record.original_question: Given a homogeneous polynomial P with integer coefficients, determine whether the equation P(x1, ..., xn) = 0 has a nonzero integer solution, meaning an integer solution different from (0, ..., 0).

evidence.quote: For homogeneous equations, Problem 4 reduces to the following question.
Problem 5. Given a homogeneous polynomial P with integer coefficients, determine whether equation (1) has an integer solution (x1, . . . , xn) != (0, . . . , 0).

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $P \in \mathbb{Z}[x_1, \dots, x_n]$ be a homogeneous polynomial in $n$ variables with integer coefficients (i.e., every monomial of $P$ has the same total degree). Provide an algorithm which, given as input any such $P$ (with $n$ and the degree arbitrary), decides whether there exists $(x_1, \dots, x_n) \in \mathbb{Z}^n \setminus \{(0, \dots, 0)\}$ such that
$$P(x_1, \dots, x_n) = 0,$$
or prove that no such algorithm exists.
artifact.status_search_result: Deciding whether a homogeneous integer polynomial has a nontrivial integer zero is equivalent (by clearing denominators and dehomogenizing) to deciding whether an arbitrary polynomial equation has a rational solution, i.e., Hilbert's tenth problem over the rationals. While Hilbert's tenth problem over $\mathbb{Z}$ was shown undecidable by Matiyasevich (1970), the analogous question over $\mathbb{Q}$ — equivalently, the homogeneous version over $\mathbb{Z}$ — remains a well-known open problem.

status_evidence.title: Hilbert's tenth problem - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: Extensions of Hilbert's tenth problem to other rings, in particular Q, remain open.
status_evidence.claim: The decidability of Diophantine equations over the rationals (equivalent to the homogeneous case over Z) is open.

status_evidence.title: Hilbert's Tenth Problem: Refinements and Variants (Gasarch)
status_evidence.snippet: Hilbert's tenth problem over Q is open and may yet lead to number theory of interest.
status_evidence.claim: The rational/homogeneous variant of Hilbert's 10th problem is still open.
